Today’s Daily Battle

One verse. Plain words. For anyone.

Psalm 102:17 (KJV)

“He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.”

In simpler words

When he has given ear to the prayer of the poor, and has not put his request on one side.

What was going on

An afflicted cry that becomes hope: the psalmist pours out his trouble, then trusts God will arise and build Zion. The verse: He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.

What it means

He hears the prayer of the destitute. He does not despise the cry of the one who has nothing to bargain with.

What was going on: An afflicted cry that becomes hope: the psalmist pours out his trouble, then trusts God will arise and build Zion. What was going on

Who’s talking?

An afflicted psalmist — a prayer of the overwhelmed (untitled in the KJV)

Who hears this?

The destitute who still pray — and you when you have nothing to bargain with

How it relates today (2026)

How it relates to you right now

One honest step, just for today: Ask once more with these words before you try to fix it: “He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.”

Say this if you want to. If words aren’t there today, that’s okay.

A simple prayer:
Lord, hear this as my whole request: “He will regard the prayer of the destitute, and not despise their prayer.” In Jesus’ name, Amen.

      Why This Exists

      Hey. Born in Dallas, raised in West Tennessee — Union City, Martin, and Memphis. Grew up where the blues play loud and the nights feel longer than they should.

      I built this because I needed it. Not some shiny app with streaks and badges—just a steady place to grab one verse when everything else was screaming. Scripture didn’t fix me overnight. It just kept showing up: “Be still,” “Cast it,” “You’re held.” And slowly, that was enough.

      Prayers and notes stay on your device unless you choose to sync. Privacy.

      Smart enough to hear “survival” and hand you Isaiah 43:2 like it’s waiting for you. Plans that say “Hey, 7 days? Let’s do 14” instead of “Start over.” Audio that reads it back—because some mornings, hearing beats reading.

      This isn’t about being perfect. It’s about showing up. If you’re fighting something right now—fear, grief, bills, loneliness—grab a verse. Breathe. You’re not solo. And if this helps even one person feel that? That’s why I keep building.

      Thanks for being here.

      Want to say thanks? Support this quiet place—keeps the verses coming.

        David & Goliath
        
      
        1 Samuel 17 — read-aloud, KJV heart
        
      
        
        
        David and Goliath — 1 Samuel 17. Goliath was a huge giant. He shouted at God’s army every day. Everyone was scared — except David.
        
        
        David was young and small, but he knew God. He said, “Who is this giant? The Lord will deliver him into my hand.” David ran toward Goliath with a sling and five stones. He swung once — and the stone hit Goliath. The giant fell. God gave David the victory!
        
        
        For you: Your giants might be fear, worry, or someone who hurts you. God is bigger. Trust Him and be brave.
        
        
        “The battle is the LORD’s.” — 1 Samuel 17:47 (KJV)
        
        
        Remember: No problem is too big when God is on your side.
